story.title: Houthis Claim Missile Attack on Saudi Arabia Amid Escalating Tensions
story.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for a missile attack targeting Saudi oil facilities in Jizan. This attack comes as tensions escalate in the region, with the Houthis also announcing a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump is considering further military strikes on Iran in response to the ongoing conflict.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
timeline_highlights.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to target Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for any attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.
key_facts: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure for each ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 international armed conflict centered on Iran, the United States and Israel, with effects extending across the Persian Gulf and neighboring states. U.S. combat operations began on February 28, 2026; the conflict has also made security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a central issue.

facts.label: Start date
facts.value: The United States notified the UN Security Council that it commenced combat operations against Iran on February 28, 2026; U.S. energy officials likewise identify military action on that date as the point after which Hormuz traffic was effectively disrupted.

facts.label: Principal parties and stated U.S. purpos
facts.value: In its UN notification, the United States said it was acting in cooperation with Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz. These are the U.S. government's stated objectives, not an independent legal finding.

facts.label: Legal position asserted by the United St
facts.value: The United States characterized its operations as necessary and proportionate self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter, including collective self-defense of Israel.

facts.label: Why the Strait of Hormuz matters
facts.value: The strait lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. In the first half of 2025, about 20.9 million barrels per day of oil—roughly one-fifth of global petroleum-liquids consumption—moved through it, while alternative routes could replace only part of disrupted flows.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers chosen developments on July 22-23, 2026—including military threats, U.S. war-powers action and oil-market effects—and does not attempt to provide a complete account of the conflict, diplomacy, or humanitarian consequences.

explore_lenses.label: Was the Aramco attack independently confirmed?
explore_lenses.title: Claimed strike, limited official confirmation
explore_lenses.summary: The Houthis said they struck Aramco facilities in Jizan and Yanbu with missiles and drones, but the reported impacts had not been independently verified as of July 25. Saudi authorities confirmed emergency alerts in the affected areas but did not publicly confirm damage to oil facilities.

claims.text: Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group fired ballistic and cruise missiles and drones at Aramco facilities in Jizan and Yanbu; CBS reported that the claimed strikes and their success could not be independently verified.
Saudi Civil Defense issued and later lifted alerts over a "potential danger" in Jizan and Yanbu, without publicly specifying the threat or reporting confirmed damage or casualties.
Saudi Arabia had not immediately commented on the Houthi Telegram claim that fires were caused in Jizan, according to SBS reporting.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the Red Sea blockade matter?
explore_lenses.title: A second risk to Saudi export routes
explore_lenses.summary: The Houthi maritime threat matters because Saudi oil exports have been using the Red Sea route to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz. Attacks also put civilian crews and commercial shipping at risk beyond the immediate Saudi-Houthi conflict.

claims.text: Associated Press reported that Saudi Arabia had recently been exporting about 4 million barrels of oil a day through Yanbu, a Red Sea port, to blunt the effects of the Strait of Hormuz closure.
The Houthis said their Bab el-Mandeb blockade remained in force after earlier attacks on two Saudi-flagged commercial tankers; CBS reported there had been no further ship strikes since then.

IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez said reported Red Sea attacks endanger seafarers, commercial routes, the marine environment and global supply chains, and called de-escalation the only solution.

The Houthi threat could increase shipping disruption if vessels reroute or operators judge the route too risky; this is an inference supported by the IMO warning that continued attacks risk disrupting commercial routes and supply chains.

explore_lenses.label: Is Washington escalating or negotiating?
explore_lenses.title: Trump kept both military and diplomatic paths open
explore_lenses.summary: President Trump had not announced a decision on a broader strike against Iran as of July 25. His public remarks described continued talks with Tehran while also maintaining that U.S. forces were prepared to intensify operations.

claims.text: Trump said he had not decided whether to hit Iran more forcefully and said Tehran was being more serious in talks with Washington, according to SBS's report of his Oval Office remarks.

Trump described two possible paths: continuing or intensifying military operations, or pursuing what he called a smarter strategy of making a deal; he also said the United States was "locked and loaded."
CBS reported no new U.S. strikes on Iran overnight July 25 after 13 consecutive nights of reported attacks, an apparent operational pause rather than a publicly announced settlement.
Trump's comments indicate that either renewed heavy strikes or a negotiated arrangement remained possible, but he supplied no timeline or publicly stated terms for either outcome.

related_stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Causes Major Fire at Saint Petersburg Warehouse
related_stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike ignited a significant fire at a Wildberries warehouse near Saint Petersburg on July 24. The blaze produced thick smoke that spread across the city and led to temporary disruptions at Pulkovo Airport, as reported by Russian authorities.

related_stories.title: Casualties Reported in Strikes on Holiday Camp and Drone Exhibition in Ukraine
related_stories.summary: At least 11 people have been reported killed in recent strikes involving both Ukrainian and Russian forces. This includes a Russian missile attack that resulted in at least 10 fatalities at a drone exhibition near Kyiv, which was attended by key figures from the Ukrainian defense sector. Additionally, Ukrainian attacks on a Russian-controlled area reportedly resulted in at least eight fatalities.

related_stories.title: UN Human Rights Chief Secures Second Term Amidst Opposition
related_stories.summary: Volker Turk has been re-elected as the UN human rights chief for a second four-year term, receiving 144 votes in favor against 10 opposed, with notable objections from the United States, Israel, and Russia. This decision reflects a significant endorsement from the UN General Assembly despite the dissenting voices.

related_stories.title: Mass Evacuations in France and Spain Due to Widespread Wildfires
related_stories.summary: Wildfires in southwestern France and Spain have forced the evacuation of over 250,000 people. Authorities in both countries are responding to the crisis, with France appealing for international assistance and Spain declaring a national emergency. The fires have been exacerbated by extreme heat and strong winds, leading to significant destruction and ongoing danger in the affected regions.
